entities.title: Set up the project
entities.summary: An npm project in games/tabletop laid out like Gambit, with its Worker, database and deploy.
acceptanceCriteria: package.json with typecheck, build (esbuild), test and deploy scripts; npm test passes on an empty suite.

Layout: shared/ (protocol types and turn logic, used by page and Worker), worker/ (index.ts, api.ts, auth.ts, db.ts, mail.ts, table.ts, schema.sql), src/ (the page), cartridges/ (AssemblyScript sources), test/.
wrangler.jsonc: the route on icelander.net, the ACCOUNTS service binding and ACCOUNTS_JWKS, the TableRoom Durable Object, the D1 database tabletop, static assets.
tabletop added to the Deploy workflow's choice list and to docs/database-migrations.md's table.
README.md says what each file does, how to develop with DEV_LOGIN and two browsers, and the owner's one-time set-up (D1, Resend, TURN key).
AGENTS.md and the root README list the app.

origin.description: The owner asked for a plan for a TypeScript web app on icelander.net where friends invited by email play a board game shipped as a WebAssembly binary, with chat, voice chat, a turn indicator, an end-turn button and wins the players acknowledge; the rules come later.

relationships.description: Users, invitations, mail and the room are copied from Gambit; the shared kit would let both use one copy.

entities.title: Sign-in, tables and invitations
entities.summary: Sign in through icelander.net, create a table for a cartridge, invite friends by email, accept or decline, and keep contacts.
acceptanceCriteria: worker/auth.ts uses vendor/icelander-auth exactly as Gambit's does; users are keyed by address in tabletop's users table.
POST api/tables creates a table (cartridge id and SHA-256 pinned) with its creator as host in seat 0.
POST api/tables/:id/invitations takes addresses, stores them, emails each through Resend with a link (?invite=ID), and returns the link when mail is off.
The invited address sees open invitations on the home screen and from the link, and accepts (takes the next free seat) or declines.
The host can reorder seats or shuffle them, and starts the game once the cartridge's minimum is seated.
Contacts: everyone a player has sat at a table with is offered when inviting.
API tests on the in-memory SQLite stand-in (as Gambit's test/fake-d1.ts) for every route, including someone else's address taking a seat (refused).

entities.title: The cartridge format, its loader and its build
entities.summary: Version 1 of the cartridge contract, a build that packs a board, pieces and rules into an AssemblyScript module, and a loader that runs it sandboxed.
acceptanceCriteria: cartridges/build.mjs turns cartridges/<id>/ (manifest.json, assets/, rules.md) into an AssemblyScript module with the blobs as static data, compiles it with asc, and writes dist/cartridges/<id>/<sha256>.wasm plus an index of the published cartridges.
src/cartridge/ loads a cartridge in a Web Worker: checks the hash, refuses any import other than env.abort, checks tt_abi, validates the manifest, and returns the blobs as object URLs.
The page's Content-Security-Policy allows wasm-unsafe-eval and nothing remote.
Tests: a malformed manifest, a wrong hash, an extra import and an unknown ABI version are each refused with a clear message.

entities.title: The first board game
entities.summary: One real cartridge, with original artwork and its rules text, to prove the format end to end.
acceptanceCriteria: cartridges/<id>/ holds the manifest, the board and piece art (SVG) and rules.md; provenance of every asset is written down.
It builds to one .wasm under 1 MiB and loads in the page, showing the board, the pieces at their start and the rules.

entities.title: The live table: board, turns and the end-turn button
entities.summary: One Durable Object per table that holds its state, accepts actions one at a time, and sends every change to every player over a WebSocket.
acceptanceCriteria: worker/table.ts: a TableRoom Durable Object built like Gambit's GameRoom (RoomCore without the object, for tests; hibernating WebSockets; actions queued one at a time).
State: seats in order, the current seat, a turn number, and each piece's position; saved to D1 after every action, with a version number so a stale write is refused.

Actions: move-piece (only the current player; within the board), undo-last (proposed and accepted by the player who moved), end-turn {turn} (only the current player, only if turn matches, so a double press passes once), pass-for {seat} (host only, only for a disconnected player).

The page draws the board and pieces on a canvas scaled to the window and to touch, shows the seats with the current player highlighted, a "Your turn" banner and tab title, and the "I'm done with this turn" button, enabled only on your turn.
Presence: who is connected, shown by each seat; reconnecting gets the whole state.
Every action goes in the table's transcript (table_events) with its time and who did it.
Tests: turn order wraps and skips no one; end-turn from the wrong player, with an old turn number, or twice, changes nothing; a move off-turn is refused.

entities.title: Chat
entities.summary: Messages at the table, delivered live and kept in the transcript.
acceptanceCriteria: A chat action (1–500 characters, trimmed) goes through the TableRoom like any other action and is broadcast to everyone.
The chat panel shows names, pictures and times, and the turn changes inline, as Gambit's transcript does.
History on (re)connect: the last 200 messages; older ones on scroll.
A simple rate limit (10 messages in 10 seconds per player).

entities.title: Voice chat
entities.summary: WebRTC audio between the players at a table, signalled over the table's WebSocket, relayed through Cloudflare TURN when needed.
acceptanceCriteria: GET api/ice returns short-lived ICE servers (STUN, and TURN credentials minted by the Worker with the TURN_KEY_ID and TURN_KEY_API_TOKEN secrets), only to signed-in players at a table.
The TableRoom relays signal messages (offer, answer, ICE candidate) from one connected player to another at the same table, never storing them.

src/voice.ts keeps one RTCPeerConnection per other player in the voice chat (perfect-negotiation pattern, so two players joining at once settle), audio only, echo cancellation and noise suppression on.
Controls: join, leave, mute; each seat shows in-voice, muted and speaking (from an AnalyserNode), and each other player's volume can be turned down.
Leaving the page or losing the socket closes the connections; rejoining reconnects.
Tested in two Chromium instances with fake audio devices (--use-fake-device-for-media-stream).

entities.title: Results, acknowledgements and the win record
entities.summary: Players propose who won; the others acknowledge or dispute, then or later; acknowledged results make the win record.
acceptanceCriteria: Any seated player can mark the game finished and propose a result: one or more winners, or no winner.
Each other player is asked to acknowledge or dispute it, on the table and on their home screen, for as long as it is pending; a dispute rejects it and anyone may propose again.
When every other player has acknowledged, the result is confirmed, stored, and written in the transcript; until then nothing counts.
A stats page: each player's games, wins and pending results per cartridge, and head to head with each friend.
Tests: a result counts only after the last acknowledgement; a dispute rejects it; a player not at the table cannot acknowledge; a proposal for a table that already has a confirmed result is refused.

entities.title: Test end to end, document and deploy
entities.summary: A two-browser end-to-end test, the .dev views, and the first deploy.
acceptanceCriteria: A Playwright test with DEV_LOGIN: two players, an invitation, a seat each, three turns with moves, a chat message, voice with fake devices, a proposed and acknowledged result.

The .dev folders describe what was built (component, deployment and state diagrams for the TableRoom and the result; use cases and journeys), with actors in Actors/; this plan's records are moved to done or deleted.
The owner's set-up done: D1 database created and its schema applied, Resend sender, TURN key; then a merge deploys it.
